newsitem.title: INDIA: Motorola, Alcatel in India deals.
newsitem.headline: Motorola, Alcatel in India deals.

text.p: India's Bharti Telenet Ltd has awarded contracts worth nearly $100 million to Alcatel Alsthom of France and U.S.-based Motorola Inc in its drive to build the country's first private basic phone network.
The two Western firms accounted for the lion's share of 6.3 billion rupees ($176 million) in deals that Bharti Telenet announced late on Saturday in the Indian capital.
Alcatel Alsthom's 1.75 billion rupee contract is for switching equipment, while Motorola's 1.7 billion rupee deal is for digital wireless equipment, Bharti Telenet executives told a news conference.
Bharti Enterprises is a pioneer in the telecommuncations industry in India, which is opening up the sector to competition.

It already operates India's largest cellular phone network, Bharti Cellular Ltd, in which British Telecommunications Plc has a minority stake, and is setting up the first private basic phone service network in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh.
"We will make the first phone available by November," Bharti Enterprises Ltd chairman Sunil Mittal told the news conference. "In three years, we will provide 225,000 phones in 23 cities."
Sunil Mittal and his brothers control Bharti Enterprises, whose closely held affiliate Bharti Televentures Ltd has a 51 percent stake in Bharti Telenet.
Telecom Italia SpA holds a 30 percent stake in Bharti Telenet, and India's Bharti Telecom Ltd 19 percent.

Bharti Telenet is one of the largest manufacturers of push-button telephones, and it has joint ventures with Japan's Casio Computer Co Ltd for marketing pagers and with Germany's Siemens AG for marketing cellular phones.

Mittal outlined a number of other contracts. AT&T Finolex Ltd, a joint venture between India's Finolex Cables Ltd and AT&T of the United States, won a contract for 400 million rupees for fibre optic cabling.
Optel Telecommunications Ltd signed a 200 million rupee contract for copper cable. Larsen and Toubro Ltd and Punj Lloyd each won 400 million rupee deals for civil works.
Mittal said network design and consultancy on communications systems and network management will be done by Deutsche Telekom AG's DeTeCon unit.
Other vendors including Motorola have bagged assorted contracts worth 850 million rupees, he said. "Bharti itself will make investments of 500 million rupees in real estate."

Mittal said that over the 15-year period of the government licence, Bharti Telenet will invest 40 billion rupees in Madhya Pradesh to install 2 million lines. In the first three years, the company will bring in equity of 6 billion rupees.
"We will give Madhya Pradesh an efficient, reliable communications network, comparable to the best in the world," Mittal said. ($1=35.7 rupees)
